body:
## Summary

- keep locally provisioned `@openai-curated` plugins in Codex's model-visible skill catalog by disabling the conflicting remote catalog only in the repository-scoped `CODEX_HOME`
- give capability discovery, plugin repair, `prompt-input`, and `codex exec` the same base environment and target-checkout cwd
- preserve the operator home and personal marketplaces, while keeping explicit capability failures fail-closed
- add a patch changeset, a real-CLI reproduction, and a root-cause case study

Closes #2094.

## Root cause and reproduction

With ChatGPT authentication and `remote_plugin` enabled, Codex 0.144.6 treats its remote global catalog as authoritative for the reserved `openai-curated` marketplace. During prompt construction it removes every locally configured plugin from that marketplace before merging remote installations:

- [`manager.rs` activates the remote catalog for Codex-backend auth](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5d1fbf26c43abc65a203928b2e31561cb039e06d/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/manager.rs#L474-L476)
- [`loader.rs` removes local `openai-curated` entries before the merge](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5d1fbf26c43abc65a203928b2e31561cb039e06d/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/loader.rs#L204-L217)

That explains the production contradiction: scoped config, all 14 cache payloads, and `codex plugin list` were healthy, but `prompt-input` contained only five built-in skills. Reinstallation could not repair an entry deliberately discarded at the next loader boundary.

The controlled real-CLI matrix is in `experiments/issue-2094/reproduce-curated-loader-boundary.sh`; the complete investigation is in `docs/case-studies/issue-2094/README.md`. In disposable operator, nested, and fresh homes, `remote_plugin=true` exposed only the backend's partial eight-skill bundle, while `remote_plugin=false` exposed all 14 locally materialized skills. The original production run had exposed zero remote Superpowers skills.

## Fix

When capability resolution selects any local plugin from `openai-curated`, Hive writes `features.remote_plugin = false` into that repository's scoped Codex config after syncing operator settings. No global config or target repository is changed. Non-reserved/personal marketplaces retain the operator's remote-catalog setting.

Hive now also derives one Codex base environment before preflight and reuses it for the actual execution. Every Codex-side catalog, repair, verification, and prompt command runs from the same checkout as `codex exec`.

## Config-write hardening (post-review)

Writing the override into `config.toml` is only safe if the write can never corrupt an operator's file. TOML expresses the same setting three ways — a `[features]` header table, a root-scope dotted `features.remote_plugin`, and an inline `features = { … }` — and the dotted form is the spelling Codex's own CLI documents. The first implementation appended a `[features]` table unconditionally, so those configs became duplicate-key documents that Codex refuses to load, which would have broken *every* Codex invocation for the repository instead of only the plugin.

The editor now rewrites whichever spelling exists, replaces any existing value rather than only a boolean literal, preserves a comment attached to the setting, recognizes `[features]# comment` headers, and treats table headers appearing inside multi-line strings as data.

Evidence:

- `experiments/issue-2094/toml-editor-cases.mjs` — 30 operator config shapes, every produced document parsed with a real TOML parser (python `tomllib`): 0 failures
- `experiments/issue-2094/verify-toml-editor-against-cli.mjs` — the rewritten documents fed to an unauthenticated `codex-cli 0.144.6`: 0 of 7 previously rejected shapes rejected
- `experiments/issue-2094/verify-remote-plugin-config-key.sh` — auth-free proof that `features.remote_plugin` is actually deserialized from `config.toml` (a mistyped value is rejected with `expected a boolean ... in features`), that the scoped shape loads, and that an unknown `[features]` key degrades to a no-op rather than a fatal error
- the same shapes are asserted in `tests/test-issue-2094-codex-curated-loader-boundary.mjs`

## Verification

The new `tests/test-issue-2094-codex-curated-loader-boundary.mjs` faithfully models the 0.144.6 reconciliation behavior and covers:

- valid installed/enabled metadata plus the complete 14-skill payload still disappearing at prompt assembly
- reserved versus personal marketplace behavior
- explicit and implicit `remote_plugin` configuration
- fresh and continued/restarted repository scopes without reinstall churn
- unchanged operator config, Docker mount mapping, and target cwd
- exact environment equality between `prompt-input` and the real `executeCodexCommand` launch path

Real target verification used Codex 0.144.6 inside the Docker runtime against the continued CEHR2005/GCS-TS PR #4 checkout. The fixed preflight exposed 19 skills (five built-ins plus all 14 Superpowers skills), verified all six explicit requirements without a reinstall, and an actual Codex session (`019f81b6-6903-7991-9e38-1ac7cd0700d2`) loaded `superpowers:using-superpowers` and completed `CAPABILITY_VERIFIED` without modifying the target checkout.

Local checks:

- `npm test` — all 348 selected test files passed under Node 24
- focused #2077/#2080/#2084/#2088/#2094 capability suites — passed under Node 20
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npx changeset status` — patch bump for `@link-assistant/hive-mind`
- `bash -n experiments/issue-2094/reproduce-curated-loader-boundary.sh`

This is not a visual/UI change, so screenshots are not applicable.
title: fix(2094): keep local curated plugins visible to Codex
